# parse-unknown-codegen

Writes [parse-unknown](https://github.com/wjsdev/parse-unknown) parsers from types you already have.

## Install

```sh
npm install --save-dev parse-unknown-codegen
```

TypeScript 5.0 or later. `parse-unknown` is a peer dependency: the generated files import it.

## Use

```sh
parsers src/address.ts
```

This reads every exported type alias and interface in `src/address.ts` and writes `src/address.parsers.ts` beside it, one `parseX` per type.

```ts
export type Address = {
  street: string;
  city: string;
  zip?: string;
};
```

becomes

```ts
// generated by parse-unknown-codegen from ./address.ts — do not edit
import { object, optional, type ParsersOf, string } from "parse-unknown";
import type { Address } from "./address";

export function parseAddress(value: unknown): Address {
  return object({
    street: string,
    city: string,
    zip: optional(string),
  } satisfies ParsersOf<Address>)(value);
}
```

The record is checked against your type with `satisfies`, so the compiler verifies the generator's output: a wrong or missing parser is a compile error in the generated file, never a runtime surprise.

`--out <dir>` writes the files somewhere else. `--check` writes nothing and fails if a generated file is stale, for CI.

## What it writes

| In your type | In the parser |
| --- | --- |
| `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `unknown` | `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `nil`, `unknown` |
| `"a" \| "b"`, `1 \| true \| "yes"` | `literal(["a", "b"])` |
| `T[]`, `readonly T[]`, `Array<T>` | `array(…)` |
| `Record<string, T>` | `record(…)` |
| `key?: T` | `optional(…)` |
| `T \| null` | `nullable(…)` |
| `T \| undefined` | `either(…, nothing)` |
| `A \| B` | `either(…)` |
| an object written inline | `object({ … } satisfies ParsersOf<User["settings"]>)` in place |
| another exported type | its `parseX`, from this file or imported from that file's `.parsers` |

A key that arrives under another name is tagged in a doc comment:

```ts
export type User = {
  /** @wire created-at */
  createdAt: string;
};
```

which gives `createdAt: from("created-at", string)`.

Only types written in the file it reads; a type imported from another package has no syntax there. Anything parse-unknown cannot express is refused, printed with its line and reason, and the file is not written.
